title: Overloading and overriding
context: What is the difference between overloading and overriding?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (1 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Overloading is several methods in one class with the same name and different parameter lists. The compiler picks one at compile time from the argument types. Overriding is a subclass providing its own version of an inherited instance method with the same signature. The JVM picks the version at run time from the actual object type. Overloading does not depend on the return type. Overriding needs a compatible return type, and `@Override` makes the compiler check the signature.

points.title: Compile time versus run time
points.why: Overloads are chosen by the compiler. Overrides are chosen by the object's real type at run time.

points.title: Use @Override
points.why: The annotation catches a typo in the signature that would otherwise create a new method silently.
